column1: # About This Edition after the modernising pass (John, 2026-11-02)

column2: Stevenson's text is given as he wrote it. Nothing has been modernised, abridged, or rewritten, and his punctuation, his spelling and his sea dialect are his own.
column3: Stevenson’s text is given in his own words, complete. Where an older spelling or a convention of the page would slow a reader or trip the voice, it has been brought up to date; nothing has been rewritten, and his sailors keep their own way of speaking.

column2: the Sources and Acknowledgements say more.
column3:
the Sources and Acknowledgements say more.

\n

The spelling is American throughout (color, harbor, center), compound words are written as one where we now write them so (spyglass, halfway, campfire), and a few old words in the telling are given in ours (before for ere, there for thither). Where a word has changed its meaning since Stevenson used it, the word we would use now stands in the text, and a small lettered note gives the word he wrote.
